entries.lyrics: Be-neath the cross of Je-sus I fain would take my stand, The sha-dow of a might-y rock with-in a wear-y land; A home with-in the wild-er-ness, a rest u-pon the way, From the burn-ing of the noon-tide heat, and the bur-den of the day.

entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ASSURANCE by Phoebe Palmer Knapp (1839–1908); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Bless-ed a-ssu-rance, Je-sus is mine! O what a fore-taste of glo-ry di-vine! Heir of sal-va-tion, pur-chase of God, Born of His Spi-rit, washed in His blood. This is my stor-y, this is my song, Prais-ing my Sa-viour all the day long; This is my stor-y, this is my song, Prais-ing my Sa-viour all the day long.

entries.title: Blessed Jesus at Thy Word
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune LIEBSTER JESU WIR SIND HIER by Johann Rudolph Ahle (1625–1673); words by Tobias Clausnitzer (1619–1684); translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: Bles-sed Je-sus, at Thy Word We are ga-thered all to hear Thee; Let our hearts and souls be stirred Now to seek and love and fear Thee, By Thy teach-ings sweet and ho-ly, Drawn from earth to love Thee sole-ly.

entries.title: Blest Are the Pure in Heart
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.

entries.lyrics: Blest are the pure in heart, For they shall see our God; The se-cret of the Lord is theirs; Their soul is Christ’s a-bode.

entries.title: Blest Be the Tie That Binds (Boylston)
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune BOYLSTON by Lowell Mason (1792–1872); words by John Fawcett (1740–1817).
entries.lyrics: Blest be the tie that binds Our hearts in Christ-ian love; The fel-low-ship of kin-dred minds Is like to that a-bove.

entries.title: Blest Be the Tie That Binds (Dennis)
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.

entries.lyrics: Blest be_ the tie_ that binds Our hearts_ in Christ_-ian love; The fel_-low-ship_ of kin_-dred minds_ Is like_ to that_ a-bove.

entries.title: Blind Bartimaeus

entries.lyrics: Blind Bar_-ti-mae-us at the gates Of Jer-i-cho_ in dark-ness waits: He hears the crowd;_ he hears a breath say "It is Christ_ of Naz-a-reth!"_ And calls_ in tones of a-go-ny, "O Je-sus, Je_-sus pi-ty me!"

entries.title: Bread of Heaven, on Thee We Feed
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune ARFON (Welsh Hymn Tune); words by Josiah Conder (1789–1855).
entries.lyrics: Bread of heav’n_ on_ Thee we feed, For Thy flesh is meat_ in_-deed: Ev-er_ may our souls be fed With this_ true and liv-ing Bread_; Day by day_ with_ strength sup-plied, Through the life of Him_ who_ died.

entries.title: Breathe on Me, Breath of God
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune AYLESBURY (From John Chetham's Psalmody, 1718); words by Edwin Hatch (1835–1889).
entries.lyrics: Breathe on me, breath of God, Fill me with life a-new, That I may love what Thou dost love, And do what Thou wouldst do.

entries.title: Bringing in the Sheaves
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune HARVEST by George A. Minor (1845–1904); words by Knowles Shaw (1834–1878).
entries.lyrics: Sow-ing in the mor-ning, sow-ing seeds of kind-ness, Sow-ing in the noon-tide and the dew-y eve; Wait-ing for the har-vest, and the time of reap-ing, We shall come re-joic-ing, bring-ing in the sheaves. Bring-ing in the sheaves, bring-ing in the sheaves, We shall come re-joic-ing, bring-ing in the sheaves; Bring-ing in the sheaves, bring-ing in the sheaves, We shall come re-joic-ing, bring-ing in the sheaves.

entries.title: Built on the Rock
entries.tune: KIRKEN DEN ER ET GAMMELT HUS
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune KIRKEN DEN ER ET GAMMELT HUS by Ludvig Mathias Lindeman (1812–1887); words by Nikolai Frederik Severin Grundtvig (1783–1872); translated by Carl Døving (1867–1937).
entries.lyrics: Built on the Rock the church doth stand, E-ven when stee-ples are fall-ing; Crum-bled have spires in e-very land, Bells still are chim-ing and cal-ling; Cal-ling the young and old to rest, But a-bove all the soul dis-tressed, Long-ing for rest ev-er-last-ing.

entries.title: Christ Arose
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune CHRIST AROSE by Robert Lowry (1826–1899); words by Robert Lowry (1826–1899).
entries.lyrics: Low in the grave He lay Je-sus my Sa-vior! Wait-ing the co-ming day‑ Je-sus my Lord! Up from the grave He a-rose, With a might-y tri-umph o'er His foes; He a-rose a Vic-tor from the dark do-main, And He lives for-ev-er with His saints to reign. He a-rose! He a-rose! Hal-le-lu-jah! Christ a-rose!

entries.title: Christ Is Made the Sure Foundation
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune WESTMINSTER ABBEY by Henry Purcell (1659–1695) and Ernest Hawkins (died undefined); words by ; translated by John Mason Neale (1818–1866).
entries.lyrics: Christ is made the sure Foun-da-tion, Christ the Head_ and Cor-ner-stone, Cho-sen of the Lord, and pre-cious, Bind-ing all_ the Church in one, Ho-ly Si-on’s help for ev-er, And her con-fi-dence a-lone.

entries.title: Christ Jesus Lay in Death's Strong Bands
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune CHRIST LAG IN TOBES BANDEN (From Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524); words by Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: Christ Je-sus lay in death's strong bands, For our of-fen-ses_ giv-en; But now at God's right hand He stands, And brings us life from_ Hea-ven. Where-fore let us joy-ful be, And sing to God right thank-ful-ly Loud songs of Al-le-lu__-ia! Al-le_-lu-ia!

entries.title: Christ, Whose Glory Fills the Skies
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune RATISBON (WERNER) by William Henry Havergal (1793–1870); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).
entries.lyrics: Christ, whose glo-ry fills the skies, Christ, the true, the on-ly Light, Sun of Right-eous-ness, a-rise, Tri-umph o’er the shades of night; Day-spring from on high, be near; Day-star, in my heart ap-pear.

entries.title: Christians, Awake, Salute the Happy Morn
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune YORKSHIRE by John Wainwright (died undefined); words by John Byrom (1692–1763).
entries.lyrics: Chris-tians, a-wake, sa-lute the hap-py morn, Where-on the Sa-viour of the world was born; Rise to a-dore the mys-ter-y of love, Which hosts of An-gels chant-ed from a-bove; With them the joy-ful tid-ings first be-gun Of God In-car-nate and the Vir-gin’s Son.

entries.title: Close to Thee
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune CLOSE TO THEE by Silas Jones Vail (1818–1884); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Thou my ev-er-last-ing por-tion, More than friend or life to me, All a-long my pil-grim jour-ney, Sa-viour, let me walk with Thee. Close to Thee, close to Thee, Close to Thee, close to Thee; All a-long my pil-grim jour-ney, Sa-viour, let me walk with Thee.

entries.title: Come Forth! Come on, with Solemn Song!
entries.tune: JEG HAR MIN SAG TIL GUD HJEMSTILT
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune JEG HAR MIN SAG TIL GUD HJEMSTILT by Ludvig Mathias Lindeman (1812–1887); words by Christian Friedrich Heinrich Sachse (1785–1860); translated by Jane Laurie Borthwick (1813–1897).
entries.lyrics: Come forth! come on, with sol-emn song! The road is short, the rest is long! The Lord brought here, He calls a-way: Make no de-lay, This home was for a pas-sing day.

entries.title: Come, Let Us Join Our Cheerful Songs
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune NATIVITY (LAHEE) by Henry Lahee (1826–1912); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748).
entries.lyrics: Come, let us join our cheer-ful songs With an-gels round the throne_. Ten thou-sand, thou-sand are their tongues, But all their joys are one.

entries.title: Come, Thou Almighty King
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ITALIAN HYMN by Felice de Giardini (1716–1796); words by Anonymous.
entries.lyrics: Come, Thou al-might_-y King, Help us Thy name__ to sing, Help us to praise! Fa-ther all glo-ri-ous, O’er all vic-to-ri-ous, Come and reign o-ver us, An-cient of Days!

entries.title: Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune NETTLETON (American folk hymn); words by Robert Robinson (1735–1790).
entries.lyrics: Come, Thou Fount of ev-ery bless-ing, Tune my heart to sing Thy grace; Streams of mer-cy, ne-ver ceas-ing, Call for songs of loud-est praise. Teach me_ some me-lo-dious son_-net, Sung by_ fla-ming tongues a-bove; Praise the mount! I’m fixed u-pon it, Mount of Thy re-deem-ing love.

entries.title: Come, Thou Long-Expected Jesus
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune JEFFERSON (From Southern Harmony, 1835); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).
entries.lyrics: Come, Thou_ long ex_-pect-ed_ Je-sus Born_ to_ set Thy_ peo-ple free; From our_ fears and_ sins re_-lease us, Let_ us_ find our_ rest in Thee. Is-rael's Strength and Con-sol_-a-tion, Hope of all the_ earth Thou_ art; Dear De_-sire of ev-ery_ na-tion, Joy_ of_ ev-ery_ long-ing heart.

entries.title: Come, Ye Disconsolate
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune CONSOLATOR (WEBBE) by Samuel Webbe (1740–1816); words by Thomas Moore (1779–1852) and Thomas Hastings (1784–1872).
entries.lyrics: Come, ye dis-con-so-late, wher_-'er ye lan-guish; Come to the mer-cy seat, fer-vent-ly kneel. Here bring your woun-ded hearts, here tell_ your_ an-guish; Earth_ has no sor-row that Heav'n can-not heal.

entries.title: Come, Ye Thankful People, Come
entries.source: the score on the tune's Wikipedia article (melody and underlay), which matches the tune as it is sung; not in the Open Hymnal.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune ST GEORGE’S WINDSOR by George Job Elvey (1816–1893); words by Henry Alford (1810–1871).
entries.lyrics: Come, ye thank-ful peo-ple, come, Raise the song of har-vest home: All is safe-ly gath-ered in, Ere the win-ter storms be-gin; God, our Mak-er, doth pro-vide For our wants to be sup-plied: Come to God’s own tem-ple, come, Raise the song of har-vest home.

entries.title: Comfort, Comfort Ye My People
entries.tune: FREU DICH SEHR, O MEINE SEELE
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune FREU DICH SEHR, O MEINE SEELE (From Trente Quatre Pseaumes de David, Geneva, 1551); words by Johann Olearius (Oelschlaeger) (1611–1684); translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: Com-fort, com-fort ye My peo-ple, Speak ye peace, thus saith our God; Com-fort those who sit in dark-ness, Mourn-ing 'neath their sor-row's load; Speak ye to Je-ru-sa-lem Of the peace that waits for them; Tell her that her sins I co-ver, And her war-fare now is o-ver.

entries.title: Count Your Blessings
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune BLESSINGS by Edwin O. Excell (1851–1921); words by Johnson Oatman Jr. (1856–1922).
entries.lyrics: When up-on life’s bil-lows you are tem-pest-tossed, When you are dis-cour-aged, think-ing all is lost, Count your man-y bless-ings, name them one by one, And it will sur-prise you what the Lord has done. Count your bless-ings, name them one by one, Count your bless-ings, see what God has done! Count your bless-ings, name them one by one, Count your man-y bless-ings, see what God has done.

entries.title: Creator of the Stars of Night (Conditor Alme Siderum)
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune CONDITOR ALME SIDERUM (traditional Proper Sarum Melody); words by Anonymous; translated by John Mason Neale (1818–1866).
entries.lyrics: Cre-a-tor of the stars of night, Thy peo-ple's ev-er-las-ting light, Je-su, Re-dee-mer, save us all, And hear Thy ser-vants when they call.

entries.title: Creator of the Stars of Night (Conditor Alme Siderum, Stylized)

entries.lyrics: Cre-a-tor of the stars of night, Thy peo-ple's ev-er-las-ting light, Je-su, Re-dee-mer, save us all, And hear Thy ser-vants when they call.

entries.title: Crown Him with Many Crowns
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Appendix to Hymns Ancient and Modern, 1869); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune DIADEMATA by George Job Elvey (1816–1893); words by Matthew Bridges (1800–1894).
entries.lyrics: Crown Him with man-y crowns, The Lamb up-on His throne; Hark! how the heav’n-ly an-them_ drowns All mu-sic but its own: A-wake, my soul, and sing Of Him who died for thee, And hail Him as thy match-less King Through all e-ter-ni-ty.

entries.title: Day of Wrath, O Day of Mourning
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DIES IRAE (DYKES) by John Bacchus Dykes (1823–1876); words by Thomas of Celano (13th century); translated by William Josiah Irons (1812–1883).
entries.lyrics: Day of wrath, O day of mourn-ing! See ful-filled the pro-phet's warn-ing, Heav'n and earth in ash-es burn-ing. Oh, what fear man's bo-som rend-eth When from Heav'n the Judge de-scend-eth On whose sen-tence all de-pend_-eth!

entries.title: Dear Christians, One and All Rejoice (Es Ist Gewisslich an Der Zeit)
entries.tune: ES IST GEWISSLICH AN DER ZEIT
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ES IST GEWISSLICH AN DER ZEIT (From Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533); words by Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: Dear Christ-ians, one and all re-joice, With ex-ul-ta-tion spring-ing, And with u-ni-ted heart and voice And ho-ly rap-ture sing-ing, Pro-claim the won-ders God hath done, How his right arm the vic-t'ry won; Right dear-ly it hath cost him.

entries.title: Dear Christians, One and All Rejoice (Nun Freut Euch)
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune NUN FREUT EUCH by Martin Luther (1483–1546); words by Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: Dear Christ-ians, one and all re-joice, With ex-ul-ta-tion spring_-ing, And with u-ni-ted heart and voice And ho-ly rap-ture sing_-ing, Pro-claim the won-ders God hath done, How his right arm the vic-t'ry won; Right dear-ly it hath cost_ him.

entries.title: Did You Think to Pray?
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune STOCKBRIDGE by William Oscar Perkins (1831–1902); words by Mary Ann Pepper Kidder (1820–1905).
entries.lyrics: Ere you left your room this morn-ing, Did you think to pray? In the name of Christ our Sa-vior, Did you sue for lov-ing fa-vor, As a shield to-day? O how pray-ing rests the wea-ry! Prayer will change the night to day; So when life seems dark and drea-ry, Don't for-get to pray.

entries.title: Draw Me Nearer
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune I AM THINE by William H. Doane (1832–1915); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: I am Thine, O Lord, I have heard Thy voice, And it told Thy love to_ me; But I long to rise in the arms of faith And be clos-er drawn to Thee. Draw me near-er, near-er bless-ed Lord, To the cross where Thou hast died; Draw me near-er, near-er, near-er bless-ed Lord, To Thy pre-cious, bleed-ing side.

entries.title: Eternal Father, Strong to Save
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune MELITA by John Bacchus Dykes (1823–1876); words by William Whiting (1825–1878).
entries.lyrics: E-ter-nal Fa-ther, strong to save, Whose arm hath bound the rest-less wave, Who bidd’st the might-y o-cean deep Its own ap-point-ed lim-its keep; Oh, hear us when we cry to Thee, For those in per-il on the sea!

entries.title: Evening and Morning
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DIE GÜLDNE SONNE by Johann Georg Ebeling (1637–1676); words by Paul Gerhardt (1607–1676); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: Eve-ning and mor_-ning, Sun-set and daw_-ning, Wealth, peace, and glad-ness, Com-fort in sad-ness, These are Thy works; all the glo-ry be Thine! Times wi-thout num-ber, A-wake or in slum-ber, Thine eye ob-serves us, From dan-ger pre-serves us, Cau-sing Thy mer-cy u-pon us to shine.

entries.title: Every Morning Mercies New
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune KELSO by Edward John Hopkins (1818–1901); words by Greville Phillimore (1821–1884).
entries.lyrics: Ev-'ry morn-ing mer-cies new Fall as fresh as morn-ing dew; Ev-'ry morn-ing let us pay Tri-bute_ with the ear-ly day: For Thy mer-cies, Lord, are sure; Thy com-pas-sion doth en-dure.

entries.title: Face to Face
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune FACE TO FACE by Grant Colfax Tullar (1869–1950); words by Carrie E. Breck (1855–1934).
entries.lyrics: Face to face with Christ, my Sa-viour, Face to face— what will it be, When with rap-ture I be-hold Him, Je-sus Christ who died for me? Face to face I shall be-hold Him, Far be-yond the star-ry sky; Face to face in all His glo-ry, I shall see Him by and by!

entries.title: Faith of Our Fathers
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. CATHERINE by Henri Frederick Hemy (1818–1888); words by Frederick William Faber (1814–1863) and James George Walton (1821–1905).
entries.lyrics: Faith of our fa_-thers, liv_-ing still, In spite of dun-geon, fi-re and sword; O how our hearts_ beat high_ with joy When-e'er we hear that glo_-rious Word! Faith of our fa-thers, ho-ly faith! We will be true to thee till death.

entries.title: Far, Far Away on Judea's Plains
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune FAR, FAR AWAY ON JUDEA by John Menzies MacFarlane (1833–1892); words by John Menzies MacFarlane (1833–1892).
entries.lyrics: Far, far a-way on Ju-de-a's_ plains, Shep-herds of old heard the joy_-ous_ strains:_ Glo-ry to God, glo-ry to God, Glo-ry to God in the high_-est; Peace on earth, good will to men; Peace on earth, good will to men.

entries.title: Fight the Good Fight
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DUKE STREET by John Hatton (1710–1793); words by John S. B. Monsell (1811–1875).
entries.lyrics: Fight the good fight with_ all thy_ might, Christ is thy strength, and Christ thy right; Lay hold on life,_ and_ it_ shall_ be Thy joy and crown e-ter-nal-ly.

entries.title: For All the Saints
entries.licence: Public domain. How died in 1897 and Barnby in 1896; the words and the tune are as The Hymnal, as authorized and approved for use by the General Convention of the Protestant Episcopal Church (1916) prints them, hymn 295.
entries.credit: Tune SARUM by Joseph Barnby (1838–1896); words by William Walsham How (1823–1897).
entries.lyrics: For all the saints, who from their la-bours rest,_ Who Thee by faith be-fore the_ world con-fessed, Thy Name, O Je-sus, be for ev-er blessed. Al-le-lu-ia, Al-le-lu-ia!

entries.title: For the Beauty of the Earth
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score; every note and the underlay agree with the score on Wikipedia's article, and the opening with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune DIX by Conrad Kocher (1786–1872) and William Henry Monk (1823–1889); words by Folliott Sandford Pierpoint (1835–1917).
entries.lyrics: For the_ beau-ty of the earth, For the glo-ry of the skies, For the_ love which from our birth O-ver and a-round us lies: Lord of all, to Thee we raise This our hymn of grate-ful praise.

entries.title: Forty Days and Forty Nights
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune HEINLEIN by Martin Herbst (died undefined) and Nurnberg (died undefined); words by George H. Smyttan (1822–1870).
entries.lyrics: For-ty days and for-ty nights Thou wast fast-ing in the wild; For-ty days and for-ty nights Tempt-ed, and yet un-de-filed.

entries.title: From God Shall Naught Divide Me
entries.tune: VON GOTT WILL ICH NICHT LASSEN
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune VON GOTT WILL ICH NICHT LASSEN (traditional French); words by Ludwig Helmbold (1532–1598); translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: From God shall naught di-vide me, For He is true for aye, And on my path will guide me, Who else should of-ten stray; His e-ver boun-teous hand By night and day is heed-ful And gives me what is need-ful, Wher-e'er I go or stand.

entries.title: From Heaven Above to Earth I Come
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune VOM HIMMEL HOCH (From Schumann's Geistliche Lieder, Leipzig, 1539); words by Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: From Heaven a-bove to earth I come, To bear good news to ev-ery home; Glad ti-dings of great joy I bring, Where-of I now will say_ and sing.

entries.title: From Nazareth
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune PUER NOBIS NASCITUR by Michael Praetorius (1571–1621); words by Margaret Elizabeth Munson Sangster (1838–1912).
entries.lyrics: Comes a-ny good from Na-za-reth? The scorn-ful cha_-llenge as of old Is flung on man-y'a jeer-ing breath From cloi-stered cells and marts of gold.

entries.title: Gentle Mary Laid Her Child
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune TEMPUS ADEST FLORIDUM (From Swedish Piae Cantones, 1582); words by Joseph Simpson Cook (1859–1933).
entries.lyrics: Gen-tle Ma-ry laid her Child low-ly in a man-ger; There He lay, the un-de-filed, to the world a Stran-ger: Such a Babe in such a place, can He be the Sa-vior? Ask the saved of all the race who have found His fa_-vor.

entries.title: Glorious Things of Thee Are Spoken
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score and the score on Wikipedia's article, which agree on every note and on the underlay.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune AUSTRIA by Joseph Haydn (1732–1809); words by John Newton (1725–1807).
entries.lyrics: Glo-rious things of thee are spo_-ken, Zi-on, cit-y of our_ God; He whose word can-not be bro_-ken Formed thee for His own a_-bode: On the Rock_ of A-ges found_-ed, What can shake thy sure re-pose? With sal-va-tion’s walls sur-round_-ed, Thou may’st_ smile_ at_ all thy_ foes.

entries.title: Glory to His Name
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune GLORY TO HIS NAME by John H. Stockton (1813–1877); words by Elisha A. Hoffman (1839–1929).
entries.lyrics: Down at the cross where my Sa-viour died, Down where for cleans-ing from sin I cried, There to my heart was the blood ap-plied; Glo-ry to His Name! Glo-ry to His Name,__ Glo-ry to His Name:__ There to my heart was the blood ap-plied; Glo-ry to His Name!

entries.title: Go to Dark Gethsemane
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune GETHSEMANE by Richard Redhead (1820–1901); words by James Montgomery (1771–1854).
entries.lyrics: Go to dark Geth-se-ma-ne, ye that feel the temp-ter's pow'r; Your Re-deem-er's con-flict see, watch with Him one bit-ter hour, Turn not from His griefs a-way; learn from Je-sus Christ to pray.

entries.title: God Be with You Till We Meet Again
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune GOD BE WITH YOU by William G. Tomer (1833–1896); words by Jeremiah E. Rankin (1828–1904).
entries.lyrics: God be with you till we meet a-gain, By His coun-sels guide, up-hold you, With His sheep se-cure-ly fold you, God be with you till we meet a-gain. Till we meet__, till we meet_, Till we meet at Je_-sus’_ feet; Till we meet__, till we meet_, God be with you till we meet a-gain.

entries.title: God Bless Our Native Land
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune AMERICA (From Harmonia Anglicana, 1742); words by Siegfried August Mahlmann (1771–1826); translated by Charles Timothy Brooks (1813–1883) and John Sullivan Dwight (1813–1893).
entries.lyrics: God bless our na-tive land! Firm may she e-ver stand Through storm and night; When the wild tem-pests rave, Ru-ler of wind and wave, Do Thou_ our_ coun-try save By_ Thy great might.

entries.title: God Himself Is Present
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WUNDERBARER KÖNIG by Joachim Neander (1650–1680); words by Gerhard Tersteegen (1697–1769); translated by Frederick William Foster (1760–1835) and John Miller (1756–1790).
entries.lyrics: God Him-self is pre-sent: Let us now a-dore Him, And with awe ap-pear be-fore Him. God is in His tem-ple, all with-in keep si-lence, Pro-strate lie with deep-est rev-erence. Him a-lone God we own, Him our God and Sa-vior; Praise His name for-ev-er.

entries.title: God, That Madest Earth and Heaven
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune AR HYD Y NOS (traditional Welsh); words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), William Mercer (1811–1873) and Richard Whately (1787–1863).
entries.lyrics: God, that ma-dest earth and Hea-ven, dark-ness and light; Who the day for toil hast giv-en, for rest the night; May Thine an-gel guards de-fend us, Slum-ber sweet Thy mer-cy send us; Ho-ly dreams and hopes at-tend us, all through the night.

entries.title: God, Whose Almighty Word
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ITALIAN HYMN by Felice de Giardini (1716–1796); words by John Marriott (1780–1825).
entries.lyrics: God, whose al-might_-y word Cha-os and dark__-ness heard And took their flight: Hear us, we hum-ble pray, And where the Gos-pel day Sheds not its glor-ious ray, Let there be light!

entries.title: God Will Take Care of You
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune MARTIN by Walter Stillman Martin (1862–1935); words by Civilla Durfee Martin (1866–1948).
entries.lyrics: Be not dis-mayed_ what-e'er be-tide, God will take care of you;_ Be-neath His wings_ of love a-bide, God will take care of you. God will take care of you, through ev-'ry day, o'er all the way; He will take care_ of you, God will take care_ of you.

entries.title: Good King Wenceslas
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune TEMPUS ADEST FLORIDUM (traditional spring carol); words by John Mason Neale (1818–1866).
entries.lyrics: Good King Wen-ces-las looked out On the feast of Ste-phen, When the snow lay round a-bout, Deep and crisp and e-ven; Bright-ly shone the moon that night, Though the frost was cru-el, When a poor man came in sight, Gath-’ring win-ter fu_-el.

entries.title: Guide Me, O Thou Great Jehovah
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (The Methodist Hymn Book, 1933); every note agrees with the score on Wikipedia's Cwm Rhondda article (printed there in 4/2 in A flat) and the opening with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune CWM RHONDDA by John Hughes (1873–1932); words by William Williams (1717–1791) and Peter Williams (1723–1796).
entries.lyrics: Guide me, O Thou great_ Je_-ho-vah, Pil-grim through this bar-ren land; I am weak, but Thou_ art_ might-y; Hold me with Thy_ pow’r-ful hand: Bread of heav-en, bread of heav-en, Feed me till I want no more; Feed me till_ I_ want no more.

entries.title: Hail the Day That Sees Him Rise
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune LLANFAIR by Robert Williams (1782–1818); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).
entries.lyrics: Hail the day that sees Him_ rise, Al__-le_-lu-ia! To His Throne a-bove_ the skies; Al__-le_-lu-ia! Christ, the Lamb for sin_-ners_ given, Al__-le-lu-ia! En-ters now the high-est_ heaven. Al__-le_-lu-ia!

entries.title: Hallelujah, What a Savior!
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HALLELUJAH WHAT A SAVIOR by Philip Paul Bliss (1838–1876); words by Philip Paul Bliss (1838–1876).
entries.lyrics: Man of Sor-rows! what a name For the Son of God, who came Ru-ined sin-ners to re-claim. Hal-le-lu-jah! What a Sa-vior!

entries.title: Happy the Man Who Feareth God (Wo Gott Zum Haus)
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WO GOTT ZUM HAUS (From Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533); words by Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: Hap-py the man who fear-eth God, Whose feet His ho-ly ways have trod; Thine own good hand shall nour-ish thee, And well and hap-py shalt_ thou be.

entries.title: Happy the Man Who Feareth God (Wo Gott Zum Haus, Walter)
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WO GOTT ZUM HAUS (WALTER) (From Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524); words by Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: Hap-py the man who fear_-eth God, Whose feet His ho-ly ways_ have trod; Thine own good hand_ shall nour-ish thee, And well and hap-py shalt____ thou be.

entries.title: Hark the Glad Sound
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune CHESTERFIELD by Thomas Haweis (1734–1820); words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751).
entries.lyrics: Hark, the glad sound! the Sa_-vior comes! The Sa_-vior pro_-mised long; Let ev_-ery heart_ pre-pare_ a throne, And ev_-ery voice_ a song.

entries.title: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Cummings's setting, 1857); every note agrees with the score on Wikipedia's article and the opening with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune MENDELSSOHN by Felix Mendelssohn (1809–1847) and William Hayman Cummings (1831–1915); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) and George Whitefield (1714–1770).
entries.lyrics: Hark! the her-ald an-gels sing_ Glo-ry to the new-born King; Peace on earth, and mer-cy mild,_ God and sin-ners re-con-ciled! Joy-ful, all ye na-tions, rise,_ Join the tri-umph of the skies;_ With th’an-gel-ic host pro-claim, Christ is_ born in Beth-le-hem! Hark! the her-ald an-gels sing Glo-ry_ to the new-born King.

entries.title: Hark the Sound of Holy Voices
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune O DURCHBRECHER by Johann Anastasius Freylinghausen (1670–1739); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: Hark the sound of ho-ly voi-ces, chan-ting at the crys-tal sea Hal-le-lu-ia! Hal-le-lu-ia! Hal-le-lu-ia! Lord to Thee. Mul-ti-tude which none can num-ber, like the stars in glo-ry stand Clothed in white ap-pa-rel, hol-ding palms of vic-t'ry in their hand.

entries.title: Hark, the Voice of Jesus Calling
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune GALILEAN by Joseph Barnby (1838–1896); words by Daniel March (1816–1909).
entries.lyrics: Hark, the voice of Je-sus cal-ling, "Who will go and work to-day? Fields are ripe and har-vests wait-ing, Who will bear the sheaves a-way?" Long and loud the Mas-ter calls us, Rich re-ward He of-fers free; Who will an-swer, glad-ly say-ing, "Here am I, send me, send me?"

entries.title: Have Thine Own Way, Lord
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune ADELAIDE by George C. Stebbins (1846–1945); words by Adelaide A. Pollard (1862–1934).
entries.lyrics: Have Thine own way, Lord! Have Thine own way! Thou art the Pot-ter, I am the clay. Mould me and make me af-ter Thy will, While I am wait-ing, yield-ed and still.

entries.title: He Hideth My Soul
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune KIRKPATRICK by William James Kirkpatrick (1838–1921); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: A won-der-ful Sa-viour is Je-sus my Lord, A won-der-ful Sa-viour to me; He hid-eth my soul in the cleft of the rock, Where riv-ers of plea-sure I see. He hid-eth my soul in the cleft of the rock, That sha-dows a dry, thirst-y land; He hid-eth my life in the depths of His love, And cov-ers me there with His hand, And cov-ers me there with_ His hand.

entries.title: He Keeps Me Singing
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HE KEEPS ME SINGING by Hans Engelmann (1872–1914); words by Luther Burgess Bridgers (1884–1948).
entries.lyrics: There's with-in my heart a mel-o-dy Je-sus whis-pers sweet and low,_ "Fear not, I am with thee, peace, be still," In all of life's ebb and flow. Je-sus, Je-sus, Je-sus,‑ Sweet-est name I know, Fills my ev-'ry long-ing, Keeps me sing-ing as I go.

entries.title: He Leadeth Me
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HE LEADETH ME by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by Joseph Henry Gilmore (1834–1918).
entries.lyrics: He lead-eth me, O bless-èd thought! O words with heav'n-ly_ com-fort fraught! What-e'er I do, wher-e'er I be Still_ 'tis God's hand_ that_ lead-eth me. He lead-eth me, He lead-eth_ me, By His own hand_ He_ lead-eth me; His faith-ful fol-low'r I would_ be, For by His hand_ He_ lead-eth me.

entries.title: He Was Not Willing
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HE WAS NOT WILLING by Lucy Jane Rider Meyer (1849–1922); words by Lucy Jane Rider Meyer (1849–1922).
entries.lyrics: "He was not will-ing that a-ny should per-ish"; Je-sus en-throned in the glo-ry a-bove, Saw our poor fal-len world, pi-tied our sor-rows, Poured out His life for us, won-der-ful love! Per-ish-ing, per-ish-ing! Throng-ing our path-way, Hearts break with bur-dens too hea-vy to bear: Je-sus would save, but there's no one to tell them, No one to lift them from sin and des-pair.

entries.title: He Who Would Valiant Be
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune MONKS GATE (traditional English); words by John Bunyan (1628–1688) and Percy Dearmer (1867–1936).
entries.lyrics: He_ who would val_-iant be 'gainst all dis-a-ster, Let_ him in con_-stan-cy fol-low the Mas-ter. There's no dis-cour-age_-ment shall make_ him once re-lent His first a-vowed_ in_-tent to be a pil-grim.

entries.title: Heavenly Father Send Thy Blessing
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune RIPLEY (GREGORIAN) (From Gregorian Chant); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: Heav'n-ly Fa-ther, send Thy bles-sing On Thy chil-dren ga-thered here, May they all, Thy Name con-fes-sing, Be to Thee fo-re-ver dear; May they be, like Jo-seph, lo-ving, Du-ti-ful, and chaste, and pure; And their faith, like Da-vid, pro-ving, Stead-fast un-to death en-dure.

entries.title: Heavenly Sunlight
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune SUNLIGHT by G. H. Cook (1864–1948); words by Henry J. Zelley (1859–1942).
entries.lyrics: Walk-ing in sun-light all of my jour-ney, O-ver the moun-tains, through the deep vale; Je-sus has said, I’ll nev-er for-sake thee— Pro-mise di-vine that nev-er can fail. Heav-en-ly sun-light! Heav-en-ly sun-light! Flood-ing my soul with glo-ry di-vine_; Hal-le-lu-jah! I am re-joic-ing_, Sing-ing His prais-es, Je-sus is mine!

entries.title: Here, O My Lord, I See Thee Face to Face
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune MORECAMBE by Frederick C. Atkinson (1841–1896); words by Horatius Bonar (1808–1889).
entries.lyrics: Here, O my Lord, I see Thee face to face; Here would I touch and han-dle_ things un-seen; Here grasp with firm-er hand e-ter-nal grace, And all my wea-ri-ness up-on Thee lean.

entries.title: Higher Ground
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune HIGHER GROUND by Charles Hutchinson Gabriel (1856–1932); words by Johnson Oatman Jr. (1856–1922).
entries.lyrics: I’m press-ing on the up-ward way, New heights I’m gain-ing ev-ery day; Still pray-ing as I’m on-ward bound, “Lord, plant my feet on high-er ground.” Lord, lift me up and let me stand, By faith, on Heav-en’s ta-ble-land, A high-er plane than I have found; Lord, plant my feet on high-er ground.

entries.title: Holy Bible, Book Divine
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune ALETTA by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by John Burton (1773–1822).
entries.lyrics: Ho-ly Bi-ble, book di__-vine, Pre-cious trea-sure, thou art__ mine; Mine, to tell me whence I came, Mine, to teach me what I__ am;

entries.title: Holy Ghost, with Light Divine
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune CANTERBURY by Orlando Gibbons (1583–1625); words by Andrew Reed (1787–1862) and Samuel Longfellow (1819–1892).
entries.lyrics: Ho-ly Ghost, with light di-vine Shine up-on this heart of mine; Chase the shades of night a-way, Turn the_ dark-ness in-to day.

entries.title: Holy God, We Praise Thy Name
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune TE DEUM (From Katholisches Gesangbuch, Maria Theresa, 1774); words by Ignaz Franz (1719–1790); translated by Clarence Alphonsus Walworth (1820–1900).
entries.lyrics: Ho-ly God,_ we praise_ Thy Name; Lord of all,_ we bow_ be-fore Thee! All on earth_ Thy scep_-ter claim, All in Hea-ven a-bove_ a-dore Thee; In-fin_-ite_ Thy vast do_-main, Ev-er-last_-ing is_ Thy reign.

entries.title: Holy, Holy, Holy! Lord God Almighty
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Hymns Ancient and Modern, 1861/1869); every note agrees with the score on Wikipedia's article and the opening with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune NICAEA by John Bacchus Dykes (1823–1876); words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826).
entries.lyrics: Ho-ly, ho-ly, ho-ly! Lord God Al-might-y! Ear-ly in the morn-ing our song shall rise to Thee; Ho-ly, ho-ly, ho-ly! mer-ci-ful and might-y, God in three Per-sons, bless-ed Trin-i-ty!

entries.title: Hosanna, Loud Hosanna
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ELLACOMBE (From Gesangbuch der Herzogl. Hofkapelle, Wurttemberg, 1784); words by Jeanette Threlfall (1821–1880).
entries.lyrics: Ho-san-na,_ loud ho-san_-na, the lit_-tle child-ren sang; Through pil-lared_ court and tem_-ple the love_-ly an-them rang. To_ Je-sus, Who had blessed__ them close_ fold-ed to His breast, The child-ren_ sang their prais_-es, the simp_-lest and the best.

entries.title: How Blest the Hearts
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HOLY MATRIMONY by Henry Williams Baker (1821–1877); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: How blest are hearts, which Christ the Lord Cou-ples as with a sil-ver cord, In nu-ptial u-ni-ty: That a-ni-ma-ted are by love And a-spi-ra-tions from a-bove, O Ho-ly Ghost, by Thee!

entries.title: How Can I Keep from Singing?
entries.tune: HOW CAN I KEEP FROM SINGING
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HOW CAN I KEEP FROM SINGING by Robert Lowry (1826–1899); words by F. J. Hartley (1845–1922), Robert Lowry (1826–1899) and Anonymous.
entries.lyrics: My life flows on in end-less song; A-bove earth's la-men-ta-tion. I catch the sweet, though far-off hymn that hails a new cre-a-tion; Through all the tu-mult and the strife, I hear that mu-sic ring-ing; It finds an e-cho in my soul... How can I keep from sing-ing?

entries.title: How Firm a Foundation
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune FOUNDATION (FUNK) by Joseph Funk (1778–1862); words by John Rippon (1751–1836).
entries.lyrics: How_ firm a foun-da-tion, ye saints of the Lord, Is laid for your faith in His ex-cel-lent Word! What more can He say than to you He hath said, You, who un-to Je-sus for re-fuge have fled?

entries.title: How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune ST. PETER by Alexander R. Reinagle (died undefined); words by John Newton (1725–1807).
entries.lyrics: How sweet the name of Je-sus sounds In a be-liev-er’s ear! It soothes his sor-rows, heals his wounds, And drives a-way his fear.

entries.title: I Heard the Bells on Christmas Day
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WALTHAM (CALKIN) by John Baptiste Calkin (1827–1905); words by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow (1807–1882).
entries.lyrics: I heard the bells on Christ-mas day Their old fa-mil-iar car-ols play, And wild and sweet the words re-peat Of peace on earth, good will to men.

entries.title: I Know That My Redeemer Lives
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DUKE STREET by John Hatton (1710–1793); words by Samuel Medley (1738–1799).
entries.lyrics: I know that my Re_-deem-er_ lives; What com-fort this sweet sen-tence gives! He lives, He lives,_ who_ once_ was_ dead; He lives, my ev-er liv-ing Head.

entries.title: I Know Whom I Have Believed
entries.tune: I KNOW WHOM I HAVE BELIEVED
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune I KNOW WHOM I HAVE BELIEVED by James McGranahan (1840–1907); words by Daniel Webster Whittle (1840–1901) and Elias Nathan (1840–1901).
entries.lyrics: I know not why_ God's_ won-drous grace To me He hath_ made_ known, Nor why, un-wor_-thy,_ Christ in love Re-deemed me for_ His_ own. But I know Whom I have be-liev-èd, And am per-sua-ded that He is ab-le To keep that which I've com-mit-ted Un-to Him a-gainst that day.

entries.title: I Need Thee Every Hour
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Pentecostal Hymns No. 2, 1898); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune NEED by Robert Lowry (1826–1899); words by Annie Sherwood Hawks (1835–1918) and Robert Lowry (1826–1899).
entries.lyrics: I need Thee ev-’ry hour, Most gra_-cious_ Lord; No ten-der voice like Thine Can peace_ af_-ford. I need Thee, O I need Thee; Ev-’ry hour I need Thee; O bless me now, my Sav-iour, I come_ to Thee!

entries.title: I Sing the Mighty Power of God
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ELLACOMBE (From Gesangbuch der Herzogl. Hofkapelle, Wurttemberg, 1784); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748).
entries.lyrics: I sing the_ migh-ty pow'r of God, That made_ the moun-tains rise; That spread the_ flow-ing seas a-broad, And built_ the lof-ty skies. I_ sing the wis-dom that or_-dained The_ sun to rule the day: The moon shines_ full at His com-mand, And all_ the stars o-bey.

entries.title: I Surrender All
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune SURRENDER by Winfield S. Weeden (1847–1908); words by Judson W. Van DeVenter (1855–1939).
entries.lyrics: All to Je-sus I sur-ren-der, All to Him I free-ly give; I will ev-er love and trust Him, In His pres-ence dai-ly live. I sur-ren-der all, I sur-ren-der all; All to Thee, my bless-ed Sav-ior, I sur-ren-der all.

entries.title: I Walk in Danger All the Way
entries.tune: DER LIEBEN SONNE LICH UND PRACHT
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DER LIEBEN SONNE LICH UND PRACHT (From Freylinghausen's Geistreiches Gesangbuch, Halle, 1704); words by Hans Adolf Brorson (1694–1764); translated by Ditlef Georgson Ristad (1863–1938).
entries.lyrics: I walk in dan-ger all the way; The thought shall ne-ver leave me That Sa-tan, who has marked his prey, Is plot-ting to de-ceive me. This foe with hid-den snares May seize me un-a-wares If e'er I fail to watch and pray: I walk in dan-ger all the way.

entries.title: If God Himself Be for Me
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WOODBIRD (traditional German); words by Paul Gerhardt (1607–1676); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: If God Him-self be for_ me, I may a host de-fy; For when I pray, be-fore_ me My foes, con-found-ed, fly. If Christ, my Head_ and Mas-ter, Be-friend me from a-bove, What foe or what dis-as_-ter Can drive me from His love?

entries.title: I'm but a Stranger Here
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. EDMUND (SULLIVAN) by Arthur Seymour Sullivan (1842–1900); words by Thomas Rawson Taylor (1807–1835).
entries.lyrics: I'm but a stran-ger here, Heav'n is my home; Earth is a des-ert drear, Heav'n is my home. Dan-ger and sor-row stand round me on ev-ery hand; Heav'n is my fa-ther-land,_ Heav'n is my home.

entries.title: Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (The Hymnal 1940); the harmony in the same source confirms each melody note.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune ST DENIO (Welsh melody); words by Walter Chalmers Smith (1824–1908).
entries.lyrics: Im-mor-tal, in-vis-i-ble, God on-ly wise, In light in-ac-ces-si-ble hid from our eyes, Most bless-ed, most glo-rious, the An-cient of Days, Al-might-y, vic-to-rious, Thy great name we praise.

entries.title: In Peace and Joy I Now Depart
entries.tune: MIT FRIED UND FREUD ICH FAR DAHIN
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune MIT FRIED UND FREUD ICH FAR DAHIN (From Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524); words by Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Leonard Woolsey Bacon (1830–1907).
entries.lyrics: In peace and joy I now de-part At God's dis-pos__-ing; For full of com-fort is_ my heart, Soft re-pos_-ing. So_ the Lord_ hath pro_-mised me, And death is but a slum__-ber.

entries.title: In the Garden
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune GARDEN by C. Austin Miles (1868–1946); words by C. Austin Miles (1868–1946).
entries.lyrics: I come to the gar-den a-lone, While the dew is still on the ro-ses, And the voice I hear fall-ing on my ear The Son of God dis-clo-ses. And He walks with me, and He talks with me, And He tells me I am His_ own; And the joy we share as we tar-ry there, None oth-er has ev-er known.

entries.title: In the Sweet By and By
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune SWEET BY AND BY by Joseph Philbrick Webster (1819–1875); words by Sanford Fillmore Bennett (1836–1898).
entries.lyrics: There’s a land that is fair-er than day, And by faith we can see it a-far; For the Fa-ther waits o-ver the way, To pre-pare us a dwell-ing place there. In the sweet by and by, We shall meet on that beau-ti-ful shore; In the sweet by and by, We shall meet on that beau-ti-ful shore.

entries.title: In These Our Days So Perilous
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune VERLEIH UNS FRIEDEN GNÄDIGLICH by Martin Luther (1483–1546); words by Traditional Latin and Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: In these our days so per-il-ous, Lord, peace in mer-cy send us; No God but Thee can fight for_ us, No God but Thee_ de-fend_ us; Thou our_ on-ly God and_ Sa_-vior.

entries.title: It Came upon a Midnight Clear
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune CAROL by Richard Storrs Willis (1819–1900); words by Edmund Hamilton Sears (1810–1876).
entries.lyrics: It came up-on_ the mid-night clear, That glor_-ious song_ of old, From an-gels bend_-ing near the earth, To touch their harps_ of gold; "Peace on the earth,_ good will to men, From Heav-en's all gra_-cious King." The world in so_-lemn still-ness lay, To hear the an_-gels sing.

entries.title: It Is Well with My Soul
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (The Evangelical Hymnal, 1921); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune VILLE DU HAVRE by Philip Paul Bliss (1838–1876); words by Horatio G. Spafford (1828–1888).
entries.lyrics: When peace, like a riv-er, at-tend_-eth my way, When sor-rows like sea bil-lows roll; What-ev-er my lot, Thou hast taught me to say, It is well, it is well with my soul. It is well with my soul, It is well, it is well with my soul.

entries.title: Jerusalem the Golden
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune EWING by Alexander C. Ewing (1830–1895); words by Bernard of Cluny aka. Bernard of Morlaix (12th century); translated by John Mason Neale (1818–1866).
entries.lyrics: Jer-u-sa-lem the gol-den, with milk and hon-ey blest, Be-neath thy con-tem-pla-tion sink heart and voice op-pressed. I know not, O I know not, what joys a-wait us there, What ra-dian-cy of glo-ry, what bliss be-yond com-pare.

entries.title: Jesu, Lover of My Soul
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ABERYSTWYTH (PARRY) by Joseph Parry (1841–1903); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus_, lov_-er of my soul, Let me to Thy bo_-som fly, While the_ near_-er wa-ters roll, While the_ tem-pest still is high. Hide me, O my Sav-ior_, hide, Till the storm of life is_ past; Safe in-to the ha-ven guide; Oh, re_-ceive_ my soul at last.

entries.title: Jesus Bids Us Shine
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune JESUS BIDS US SHINE by Edwin Othello Excell (1851–1921); words by Susan Warner (1819–1885).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus bids us shine with a clear, pure light, Like a lit-tle can-dle burn-ing in the night; In this world of dark-ness, we_ must_ shine, You in your small cor-ner, and I in mine.

entries.title: Jesus Calls Us o’er the Tumult
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune GALILEE (JUDE) by William Herbert Jude (1851–1922); words by Cecil Frances Alexander (1818–1895).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus calls us; o’er the tu-mult Of our life’s wild rest-less sea Day by day His sweet voice sound-eth, Say-ing, “Chris-tian, fol-low Me:”

entries.title: Jesus Came, the Heavens Adoring
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune SIEH, HIER BIN ICH, EHRENKOENIG (From Geistreiches Gesangbuch Darmstadt, 1698); words by Godfrey Thring (1823–1903).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus came, the heav'ns a-dor-ing, Came with peace from realms on high; Je-sus came for man's re-demp-tion, Low-ly came on earth to die. Al-le-lu-ia!_ Al-le-lu-ia! Came in_ deep hu-mil-i-ty.

entries.title: Jesus Christ Is Risen Today
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (after Church Praise, 1885); the harmony in the same source confirms each melody note.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune EASTER HYMN (Lyra Davidica); words by Latin Easter carol, Lyra Davidica and Charles Wesley (1707–1788).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus Christ is ris’n to-day,_ Al____-le_-lu_-ia! Our tri-um-phant ho-ly day,_ Al____-le_-lu_-ia! Who did once up-on the cross Al____-le_-lu_-ia! Suf_-fer_ to re-deem our loss._ Al_____-le_-lu_-ia!

entries.title: Jesus Christ Who Came to Save
entries.tune: JESUS CHRISTUS UNSER HEILAND, DER DEN TOD (KLUG)
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune JESUS CHRISTUS UNSER HEILAND, DER DEN TOD (KLUG) (From Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533); words by Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Leonard Woolsey Bacon (1830–1907).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus Christ, who came to save,__ And o-ver-came the grave, Is now_ a-ris_-en, And sin hath bound in pri_-son. Ky-ri' e-lei_-son.

entries.title: Jesus, in Thy Dying Woes
entries.tune: WORDS ON THE CROSS - THE LITANY
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WORDS ON THE CROSS - THE LITANY by William Henry Monk (1823–1889); words by Thomas Benson Pollock (1836–1896).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus, in Thy dy-ing woes, E-ven while Thy life-blood flows, Cra-ving par-don for Thy foes; Hear us, ho-ly Je-sus.

entries.title: Jesus Is All the World to Me
entries.tune: JESUS IS ALL THE WORLD TO ME
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune JESUS IS ALL THE WORLD TO ME by Will Lamartine Thompson (1847–1909); words by Will Lamartine Thompson (1847–1909).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus is all the world to me, My life, my joy, my all; He is my strength from day to day, With-out Him I_ would fall. When I am sad, to Him I go, No o-ther one can cheer me so; When I am sad, He makes me glad, He's my friend.

entries.title: Jesus, King of Glory
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. ALBAN by Franz Joseph Haydn (1732–1809); words by W. Hope Davison (1827–1894).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus, King of glo-ry, throned a-bove the sky, Je-sus, ten-der Sa-vior, hear Thy child-ren cry. Par-don our trans-gres-sions, cleanse us from our sin,_ By Thy Spi-rit help us heav'n-ly life to win. Je-sus, King of glo-ry, throned a-bove the sky, Je-sus, ten-der Sa-vior, hear Thy child-ren cry.

entries.title: Jesus Loves Me
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Bradbury's Golden Chain and Shower, 1866); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune JESUS LOVES ME by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by Anna Bartlett Warner (1827–1915) and William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus loves me! this I know, For the Bi-ble tells me so; Lit-tle ones to Him be-long; They are weak, but He is strong. Yes, Je-sus loves me! Yes, Je-sus loves me! Yes, Je-sus loves me! The Bi-ble tells me so.

entries.title: Jesus Paid It All
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune ALL TO CHRIST by John T. Grape (1835–1915); words by Elvina M. Hall (1820–1889).
entries.lyrics: I hear the Sa-viour say, “Thy strength in-deed is_ small; Child of weak-ness, watch and pray, Find in Me thine all in all.” Je-sus paid it all, All to Him I owe; Sin had left a crim-son stain, He washed it white as snow.

entries.title: Jesus Saves!
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune JESUS SAVES by William James Kirkpatrick (1838–1921); words by Priscilla J. Owens (1829–1907).
entries.lyrics: We have heard the joy-ful sound: Je-sus saves! Je-sus saves! Spread the tid-ings all a-round: Je-sus saves! Je-sus saves! Bear the news to ev-ery land, Climb the moun-tains, cross the waves; On-ward! ’tis our Lord’s com-mand; Je-sus saves! Je-sus saves!

entries.title: Jesus, Saviour, Pilot Me
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune PILOT by John Edgar Gould (1821–1875); words by Edward Hopper (1816–1888).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus, Sav-iour, pi_-lot me, O-ver life’s tem-pes-tuous sea; Un-known waves be-fore me roll, Hid-ing rock and treach-’rous shoal; Chart and com-pass come_ from Thee: Je-sus, Sav-iour, pi-lot me!

entries.title: Jesus Shall Reign
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DUKE STREET by John Hatton (1710–1793); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748).

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. FLAVIAN (From Day's Psalter, 1563); words by Claudia Frances Ibotson Hernaman (1838–1898).
entries.lyrics: Lord, who through-out these for-ty days For us didst fast and pray, Teach us with Thee to mourn our sins And close by Thee to stay.

entries.title: Love Lifted Me
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune SAFETY by Howard E. Smith (1825–1898); words by James Rowe (1865–1933).
entries.lyrics: I was sink-ing deep in sin, Far from the peace-ful shore, Ve-ry deep-ly stained with-in, Sink-ing to rise no more; But the Mas-ter of the sea Heard my de-spair-ing cry, From the wa-ters lift-ed me— Now safe am I. Love lift-ed me, Love lift-ed me, When noth-ing else could help, Love lift-ed me_; Love lift-ed me, Love lift-ed me, When noth-ing else could help, Love lift-ed me_.

entries.title: May God Bestow on Us His Grace

entries.lyrics: May God be-stow on us__ His grace, With bless-ings rich pro-vide___ us, And may the bright-ness of__ His face To life e-ter-nal guide___ us That we His sa-ving health may know, His gra-cious will and plea-sure, And al-so to the hea-then show Christ's rich-es with-out mea-sure And un-to God con-vert_ them.

entries.title: Mine Eyes Have Seen the Glory
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune BATTLE HYMN (traditional American camp-meeting tune); words by Julia Ward Howe (1819–1910).
entries.lyrics: Mine_ eyes have seen the glo-ry of the com-ing of the Lord: He is tramp-ling out the vin-tage where the grapes of wrath are stored; He hath loosed the fate-ful light-ning of His ter-ri-ble swift sword: His truth is march-ing on. Glo-ry! glo-ry! Hal-le-lu-jah! Glo-ry! glo-ry! Hal-le-lu-jah! Glo-ry! glo-ry! Hal-le-lu-jah! His truth is march-ing on.

entries.title: More Love to Thee
