entries.lyrics: Ye ser-vants of God, your Mas-ter pro-claim, And pub-lish a-broad his won_-der-ful name; The name all-vic-to-rious of Je-sus ex-tol, His king-dom is glo-rious and rules o_-ver all.

entries.title: Yield Not to Temptation
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune FORTITUDE (PALMER) by Horatio Richmond Palmer (1834–1907); words by Horatio R. Palmer (1834–1907).
entries.lyrics: Yield not to temp-ta-tion, for yield-ing is sin; Each vict’-ry will help you some oth-er to win; Fight man-ful-ly on-ward, dark pas-sions sub-due; Look ev-er to Je-sus, He will car-ry you through. Ask the Sa-viour to help you, Com-fort, strength-en, and keep you; He is will-ing to aid you, He will car-ry you through.

aberystwyth parry: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ABERYSTWYTH (PARRY) by Joseph Parry (1841–1903); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).

Je-sus_, lov_-er of my soul, Let me to Thy bo_-som fly, While the_ near_-er wa-ters roll, While the_ tem-pest still is high. Hide me, O my Sav-ior_, hide, Till the storm of life is_ past; Safe in-to the ha-ven guide; Oh, re_-ceive_ my soul at last.
Savior When in Dust to Thee
Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ABERYSTWYTH (PARRY) by Joseph Parry (1841–1903); words by Robert Grant (1778–1838).

Sa-vior,_ when_ in dust to Thee Low we bow th'a-dor_-ing knee, When, re_-pent_-ant, to the skies Scarce we_ lift our weep-ing eyes, O by all the pains and_ woes Suff-ered once for man be_-low, Bend-ing from Thy throne on high, Hear our_ pen_-i-ten-tial cry!
ach gott vom himmel: Look Down, O Lord, from Heaven Behold (Ach Gott Vom Himmel)

Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ACH GOTT VOM HIMMEL (From Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524); words by Martin Luther (1483–1546); translated by Frances Elizabeth Cox (1812–1897).

Look down, O Lord, from heav'n be-hold, And let thy pit-y wa_-ken! How few the flock with-in thy fold, Ne-glec-ted and for-sa_-ken! Al-most thou'lt seek for faith in vain, And those who should thy truth main-tain Thy Word from us have ta_-ken.
act gott vom himmelreiche: The Bridegroom Soon Will Call Us

Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ACT GOTT VOM HIMMELREICHE by Michael Praetorius (1571–1621); words by Johann Walther (1496–1570); translated by Matthias Loy (1828–1915).

The Bride-groom soon will call__ us, Come, all ye wed-ding guests! May not His voice ap-pall__ us, While slum-ber binds our breasts; May all our lamps be burn__-ing, And oil be found in store, That we, with Him re-turn__-ing, May o-pen find the door.
adelaide: Tune ADELAIDE by George C. Stebbins (1846–1945); words by Adelaide A. Pollard (1862–1934).
Have Thine own way, Lord! Have Thine own way! Thou art the Pot-ter, I am the clay. Mould me and make me af-ter Thy will, While I am wait-ing, yield-ed and still.
adeste fideles: Tune ADESTE FIDELES by John Francis Wade (died 1786); words by John Francis Wade (died 1786) and Frederick Oakeley (1802–1880).

O come, all ye faith-ful, joy-ful and tri-um-phant, O come ye, O come_ ye to Beth_-le-hem; Come and be-hold Him, born the King of an_-gels: O come, let us a-dore Him, O come, let us a-dore Him, O come, let us a-dore Him,_ Christ_ the Lord.
aletta: Tune ALETTA by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by John Burton (1773–1822).
Ho-ly Bi-ble, book di__-vine, Pre-cious trea-sure, thou art__ mine; Mine, to tell me whence I came, Mine, to teach me what I__ am;
alford: Tune ALFORD by John Bacchus Dykes (1823–1876); words by Henry Alford (1810–1871).

Ten thou-sand times ten thou-sand In spark-ling rai-ment bright, The ar-mies of the ran-somed saints Throng up the steeps of light: ’Tis fin-ished, all is fin-ished, Their fight with death and_ sin: Fling o-pen wide the gold-en gates, And let the vic-tors in.
all for jesus: brother-rest-from-sin-and-sorrow
Brother, Rest from Sin and Sorrow
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/brother-rest-from-sin-and-sorrow
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Anonymous.
Bro-ther, rest from sin and sor-row; Death is o'er and life is won; On thy slum-ber dawns no mor-row: Rest; thine earth-ly race is run.
christian-soldiers-in-the-conflict
Christian Soldiers in the Conflict
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/christian-soldiers-in-the-conflict
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Traditional Latin; translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925).
Chris-tian sol-diers in the con-flict! Bear the ban-ner of the cross; Rich re-ward shall crown the vic-tor, More than rec-om-pense for loss.
come-ye-people-come-adore-him
Come Ye People, Come Adore Him
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/come-ye-people-come-adore-him
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Traditional Greek; translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925).
Come ye peo-ple, come a-dore Him, God in Ho-ly Trin-i-ty; God the Fa-ther, Son, and Spir-it, Ev-er Bless-ed U-ni-ty.
fare-thee-well-our-fondly-cherished
Fare Thee Well, Our Fondly Cherished
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/fare-thee-well-our-fondly-cherished
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Anonymous.
Fare thee well, our fond-ly cher-ished! Dear, dear blos-som, fare thee well! He who lent thee hath re-called thee, Back with Him and His to dwell.
father-source-of-every-blessing
Father, Source of Every Blessing
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/father-source-of-every-blessing
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Anonymous.
Fa-ther, source of ev-ery bless-ing, Tune my heart to grate-ful lays! Streams of mer-cy, nev-er ceas-ing, Call for cease-less songs of praise.
in-the-cross-of-christ-i-glory
In the Cross of Christ I Glory
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/in-the-cross-of-christ-i-glory
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by John Bowring (1792–1872).
In the cross of Christ I glo-ry, Tow-ering o'er the wrecks of time; All the light of sa-cred sto-ry Gath-ers round its head sub-lime.
israels-shepherd-guide-me-feed-me
Israel's Shepherd, Guide Me, Feed Me
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/israels-shepherd-guide-me-feed-me
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Edward Bickersteth (1786–1850).
Is-rael's Shep-herd, guide me, feed me. Through my pil-grim-age be-low, And be-side the wa-ters lead me, Where thy flock re-joic-ing go.
israels-shepherd-guide-us-feed-us
Israel's Shepherd, Guide Us, Feed Us
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/israels-shepherd-guide-us-feed-us
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Edward Bickersteth (1786–1850).
Is-rael's Shep-herd, guide us, feed us, Through our pil-grim-age be-low, And be-side the wa-ters lead us, Where Thy flock re-joic-ing go.
lamb-of-god-we-fall-before-thee
Lamb of God, We Fall Before Thee
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/lamb-of-god-we-fall-before-thee
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Joseph Hart (1712–1768).
Lamb of God, we fall be-fore Thee, Hum-bly trust-ing in Thy cross; That a-lone be all our glo-ry, All things else are on-ly dross.
light-serene-of-holy-glory
Light Serene of Holy Glory
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/light-serene-of-holy-glory
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Traditional Greek; translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925).
Light se-rene of ho-ly glo-ry From th'Im-mor-tal Fa-ther poured, Ho-ly Thou, O Bless-ed Je-sus, Ho-ly, Bless-ed, Christ the Lord.
one-sweet-flower-has-drooped-and-faded
One Sweet Flower Has Drooped and Faded
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/one-sweet-flower-has-drooped-and-faded
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Robert Cassie Waterston (1812–1893).
One sweet flower has drooped and fad-ed, One sweet in-fant's voice has fled, One fair brow the grave has shad-ed, One dear school mate now is dead.
savior-all-my-sins-confessing
Savior, All My Sins Confessing
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/savior-all-my-sins-confessing
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Thomas Haweis (1734–1820).
Sa-vior, all my sins con-fes-sing, Gra-cious hear me when I cry; Give through faith the pro-mised bless-ing, Free-ly, ful-ly jus-ti-fy.
saviour-i-my-cross-have-taken
Saviour! I My Cross Have Taken
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/saviour-i-my-cross-have-taken
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Anonymous.
Sa-viour! I my cross have ta-ken, All to leave, and fol-low thee; Though by all things else for-sa-ken, Thou shall my Re-deem-er be.
sister-thou-wast-mild-and-lovely
Sister, Thou Wast Mild and Lovely
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/sister-thou-wast-mild-and-lovely
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Samuel Francis Smith (1808–1895).
Sis-ter, thou wast mild and love-ly, Gen-tle as the sum-mer breeze, Plea-sant as th'air of e-ve-ning, When it floats a-mong the trees.
theories-which-thousands-cherish
Theories, Which Thousands Cherish
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/theories-which-thousands-cherish
Tune ALL FOR JESUS by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Robert Cassie Waterston (1812–1893).
The-o-ries, which thou-sands cher-ish, Pass like clouds that sweep the sky; Creeds and dog-mas all may per-ish; Truth her-self can nev-er die.
all saints new: all-natures-works-his-praise-declare
All Nature's Works His Praise Declare
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/all-natures-works-his-praise-declare
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Henry Ware Jr. (1794–1843).

All na-ture's works his praise de-clare To whom they all be-long; There is a voice in ev-ery star, In ev-ery breeze a song. Sweet mu-sic fills the world a-broad With strains of love and power; The storm-y sea sings praise to God The thun-der and the shower.
amid-surrounding-gloom-and-waste
Amid Surrounding Gloom and Waste
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/amid-surrounding-gloom-and-waste
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Edwin Hubbell Chapin (1814–1880).

A-mid sur-round-ing gloom and waste, From na-ture's face we flee; And in our fear and won-der haste O na-ture's life, to thee! Thy ways are in the might-y deep; In tem-pests as they blow; In floods that o'er our trea-sures sweep; The light-ning; and the snow.
father-when-oer-our-trembling-hearts
Father, When O'er Our Trembling Hearts
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/father-when-oer-our-trembling-hearts
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch (1809–1870).

Fa-ther, when o'er our trem-bling hearts Doubt's sha-dows gath-ering brood, When faith in Thee al-most de-parts, And gloomi-est fears in-trude; For-sake us not, O God of grace, But send those fears re-lief; Grant us a-gain to see Thy face; Lord, help our un-be-lief!
god-of-all-grace-and-majesty
God of All Grace and Majesty
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/god-of-all-grace-and-majesty
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).

God of all grace and maj-es-ty, Su-preme-ly great and good! If I have mer-cy found with thee, Through the a-ton-ing blood, The guard of all thy mer-cies give, And to my par-don join A fear lest I should ev-er grieve The gra-cious Spirit di-vine.
i-looked-upon-the-righteous-man
I Looked upon the Righteous Man
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/i-looked-upon-the-righteous-man
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Anonymous.

I looked up-on the right-eous man, And saw his part-ing breath, With-out a strug-gle or a sigh, Se-rene-ly yield to death: There was no an-guish on his brow, Nor ter-ror in his eye; The spoil-er aimed a fa-tal dart, But lost the vic-to-ry.
jesus-my-master-and-my-lord
Jesus, My Master and My Lord
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/jesus-my-master-and-my-lord
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).

Je-sus, my Mas-ter and my Lord, I would thy will o-bey, Hum-bly re-ceive thy warn-ing word, And al-ways watch and pray. My con-stant need of watch-ful prayer I dail-y see and feel, To keep me safe from ev-ery snare Of sin, and earth, and hell.
lord-soothe-my-anxious-troubled-soul
Lord, Soothe My Anxious, Troubled Soul
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/lord-soothe-my-anxious-troubled-soul
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Traditional Greek; translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925).

Lord, soothe my anx-ious, trou-bled soul, And bid its doubt-ing cease, Speak to the crest-ed waves that roll, To sink in qui-et peace; And bring me to a place of rest, A ha-ven calm and still, Where ev-ery soul by sin dis-tressed, May dwell se-cure from ill.
now-gird-your-patient-loins-again
Now Gird Your Patient Loins Again
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/now-gird-your-patient-loins-again
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by William Croswell (1804–1851).

Now gird your pa-tient loins a-gain, Your wast-ing torch-es trim! The chief of all the sons of men, Shall we not wel-come him? Fill all his courts with sa-cred songs, And from the tem-ple wall Wave gar-lands o'er the joy-ful throngs That crowd his fes-ti-val!
o-where-are-kings-and-empires-now
O Where Are Kings and Empires Now
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/o-where-are-kings-and-empires-now
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Arthur Cleveland Coxe (1818–1896).

O where are kings and em-pires now Of old that went and came? But Ho-ly Church is pray-ing yet, A thou-sand years the same. Mark ye her ho-ly bat-tle-ments, And her foun-da-tions strong; And hear with-in, her sol-emn voice, And her un-end-ing song.
o-not-alone-with-outward-sign
O, Not Alone with Outward Sign
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/o-not-alone-with-outward-sign
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by John Greenleaf Whittier (1807–1892).

O, not a-lone with out-ward sign Of fear, or voice from heaven, The mes-sage of a truth di-vine, The call of God, is given; Awak-en-ing in the hu-man heart Love for the True and Right, Zeal for the Christ-ian's bet-ter part, Strength for the Christ-ian's fight.
o-who-shall-see-the-glorious-day
O, Who Shall See the Glorious Day
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/o-who-shall-see-the-glorious-day
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Thomas Moore (1779–1852).

O, who shall see the glo-rious day, When, throned on Zi-on's brow, The Lord shall rend the veil a-way That hides the na-tions now! When earth no more be-neath the fear Of his re-buke shall lie, When pain shall cease, and ev-ery tear Be wiped from ev-ery eye!
oh-not-alone-with-outward-sign
Oh! Not Alone with Outward Sign
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/oh-not-alone-with-outward-sign
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by John Greenleaf Whittier (1807–1892).

Oh! not a-lone with out-ward sign, Of fear, or voice from heaven, The mes-sage of a truth di-vine, The call of God, is given; Awak-en-ing in the hu-man heart, Love for the true and right, Zeal for the Christ-ian's bet-ter part, Strength for the Christ-ian's fight.
our-pathway-oft-is-wet-with-tears
Our Pathway Oft Is Wet with Tears
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/our-pathway-oft-is-wet-with-tears
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Bernard Barton (1784–1849).

Our path-way oft is wet with tears, Our sky with clouds o'er-cast, And world-ly cares and world-ly fears Go with us to the last; Not to the last! God's word hath said, Could we but read a-right: O pil-grim! lift in hope thy head, At eve it shall be light!
the-aged-sufferer-waited-long
The Aged Sufferer Waited Long
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/the-aged-sufferer-waited-long
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch (1809–1870).

The aged suf-fer-er wait-ed long Up-on Be-thes-da's brink; Till hopes, once ris-ing warm and strong, Be-gan in fears to sink; And hea-vy were the sighs he drew, And fer-vent was his prayer, For he, with safe-ty full in view, Still lan-guished help-less there.
thy-servants-in-the-temple-watched
Thy Servants in the Temple Watched
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/thy-servants-in-the-temple-watched
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Anonymous.

Thy ser-vants in the tem-ple watched The daw-ning of the day, Im-pa-tient with its ear-liest beams Their ho-ly vows to pay; And cho-sen saints far off be-held That great and glo-rious morn, When the glad day spring from on high Aus-pi-cious-ly should dawn.
when-on-devotions-seraph-wing
When, on Devotion's Seraph Wing
https://notefusion.studio/hymns/when-on-devotions-seraph-wing
Tune ALL SAINTS, NEW by Henry Stephen Cutler (1825–1902); words by Sarah Elizabeth Miles (1807–1877).

When, on de-vo-tion's ser-aph wing, The spir-it soars a-bove, And feels Thy pre-sence, Fa-ther, Friend, God of e-ter-nal love! The joys of earth, how swift they fade Be-fore that liv-ing ray, Which gives to the rapt soul a glimpse Of pure and per-fect day!
all the way: All the Way My Saviour Leads Me
Tune ALL THE WAY by Robert Lowry (1826–1899); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).

All the way my Sav-ior leads me, What have I to ask be-side? Can I doubt His ten-der mer-cy, Who through life has been my Guide? Heav’n-ly peace, di-vin-est com-fort, Here by faith in Him to dwell! For I know, what-e’er be-fall me, Je-sus do-eth all things well; For I know, what-e’er be-fall me, Je-sus do-eth all things well.
all things bright: Tune ALL THINGS BRIGHT by William Henry Monk (1823–1889); words by Cecil Frances Alexander (1818–1895).

All things bright and beau-ti-ful, All crea-tures great and small, All things wise and won-der-ful, The Lord God made them all. Each lit-tle flower that o-pens, Each lit-tle bird that sings, He made their glow-ing col-ours, He made their ti-ny wings. All things bright and beau-ti-ful, All crea-tures great and small, All things wise and won-der-ful, The Lord God made them all.
all to christ: Tune ALL TO CHRIST by John T. Grape (1835–1915); words by Elvina M. Hall (1820–1889).

I hear the Sa-viour say, “Thy strength in-deed is_ small; Child of weak-ness, watch and pray, Find in Me thine all in all.” Je-sus paid it all, All to Him I owe; Sin had left a crim-son stain, He washed it white as snow.
alles ist an gottes segen: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ALLES IST AN GOTTES SEGEN by Johann Balthasar König (1691–1758); words by Anonymous; translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).

All de-pends on our pos-sess-ing God's a-bun-dant grace and bless-ing, Though all earth-ly wealth de-part. He who trusts with faith un-sha-ken In His God is not for-sa-ken And e'er keeps a daunt-less heart.
almost persuaded: Tune ALMOST PERSUADED by Philip P. Bliss (1838–1876); words by Philip P. Bliss (1838–1876).
“Al-most per-suad-ed” now to be-lieve; “Al-most per-suad-ed” Christ to re-ceive; Seems now some soul to say, “Go, Spi-rit, go Thy way, Some more con-ven-ient day On Thee I’ll call.”
america: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune AMERICA (From Harmonia Anglicana, 1742); words by Siegfried August Mahlmann (1771–1826); translated by Charles Timothy Brooks (1813–1883) and John Sullivan Dwight (1813–1893).
God bless our na-tive land! Firm may she e-ver stand Through storm and night; When the wild tem-pests rave, Ru-ler of wind and wave, Do Thou_ our_ coun-try save By_ Thy great might.
angel s story: Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by John Ernest Bode (1816–1874).

O Je-sus, I have prom-ised To serve Thee to the end; Be Thou for-ev-er near me, My Mas-ter and my Friend; I shall not fear the bat-tle If Thou art by my side, Nor wan-der from the path-way If Thou wilt be my Guide.
Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by William Chatterton Dix (1837–1898).

“Come un-to Me, ye wea-ry, And I will give you rest.” O bless-ed voice of Je-sus, Which comes to hearts op-prest! It tells of be-ne-dic-tion, Of par-don, grace, and peace, Of joy that hath no end-ing, Of love which can-not cease.
Ere God Had Built the Mountains
Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by William Cowper (1731–1800).

Ere God had built the moun-tains, Or raised the fruit-ful hills; Be-fore he filled the foun-tains That feed the run-ning rills; In me, from ev-er-last-ing, The won-der-ful I Am, Found plea-sures nev-er wast-ing, And Wis-dom is my name.
Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by Anonymous.

Go when the morn-ing shin-eth, Go when the noon is bright, Go when the eve de-cli-neth, Go in the hush of night; Go with pure mind and feel-ing, Put earth-ly thoughts a-way, And, in God's pre-sence kneel-ing, Do thou in se-cret pray.
In the Broad Fields of Heaven
Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by Anonymous.

In the broad fields of hea-ven, In th'im-mor-tal bo-wers, By life's clear riv-er dwell-ing, A-mid un-dying flo-wers, There hosts of beau-teous spi-rits, Fair child-ren of the earth, Linked in bright bands ce-les-tial, Sing of their hu-man birth.
Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by Traditional Greek; translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925).

O Son of God, a-fflic-ted, And slain for sin-ful men, My soul hath oft' de-pict-ed What Thou didst suf-fer then, The pain, the grief, the sigh-ing, The bur-den of Thy woe, The cross, the shame, the dy-ing That filled Thy life be-low.
Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by Simon Dach (1605–1659); translated by August Crull (1845–1923).

Through Je-sus’ blood and mer-it I am at peace with God; What, then, can daunt my spir-it, How-ev-er dark my road? My cou-rage shall not fail me, For God is on my side; Though hell it-self as-sail me, Its rage I may de-ride.
To Thee, My God and Saviour
Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by Anonymous.

To Thee, my God and Sa-viour, My soul ex-ult-ing sings; Re-joic-ing in thy fa-vor, Al-might-y King of kings! I'll cel-e-brate thy glo-ry With all thy saints a-bove. And tell the joy-ful sto-ry Of thy re-deem-ing love.
To Thee, O Dear, Dear Savior
Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by John Samuel Bewley Monsell (1811–1875).
